title: Entity-definition schema + migration + per-tenant registry (server column allowlist, entity cap)

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: Foundation: the entity definitions everything generates from. The server-defined per-source column allowlist added here is the security root — the entity def is otherwise an attacker-authored allowlist. No dependencies. Enhanced-review round 1 applied.

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; Second Brain hub 3ee5f890. Agent-native: no web UI. Review round 1: added a server per-source column allowlist, a per-tenant entity cap, RLS-on-migration, and deferred relationships out of v1.
background.includes: loopctl's knowledge_search retrieves CURATED articles; there is no schema-driven governed tool surface over STRUCTURED records. This story adds per-tenant entity definitions (the schema the generator + executor consume). Phase-1 backing sources are loopctl-internal only (projects/stories/epics). CRUCIAL: because the entity definition becomes the executor's field allowlist, a tenant admin must NOT be able to declare arbitrary columns of the backing table — a SERVER-defined per-source exposed-column allowlist bounds what any entity may declare.

story.as_a: a loopctl tenant admin (or an agent acting for one)
story.i_want_to: declare entity definitions (name, fields with type + filterable?/searchable?, backing source) whose fields are constrained to a server-approved column allowlist for that source, persisted per tenant
story.so_that: the generator and executor produce a governed query surface that can never expose a backing column the server did not sanction

rationale: The entity definition IS the executor's allowlist (US-30.2/30.3), and it is authored by a >= user tenant admin. Without a server-side per-source column allowlist, an admin could declare tenant_id, audit/custody, or arbitrary jsonb columns and the 'declared-fields-only' shaping would faithfully return them — a self-authored data-exfiltration path. Bounding declarable fields to a sanctioned set per backing source is the security root the whole epic rests on.

acceptance_criteria.description: Ecto schema Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Entity (table entity_definitions): tenant_id, name (unique per tenant), backing_source (Ecto.Enum, phase-1 loopctl-internal sources only), fields ({:array, :map} with per-element validation: %{name, type, filterable, searchable}), inserted_at/updated_at. tenant_id set programmatically, never cast. (Relationships are NOT persisted in v1 — see AC-30.1.6.)

A SERVER-defined per-backing-source exposed-column allowlist (code constant, e.g. %{stories: [:status, :title, :description, :epic_id, ...], projects: [...]}) lists which columns each source may expose. Changeset validation rejects any declared field whose name is not in that source's allowlist, in addition to validating type, filterable/searchable booleans, and a safe identifier regex. A tenant CANNOT declare tenant_id, audit/custody, or unsanctioned columns.

Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Registry.for_tenant/1 returns a tenant's entity definitions (scope-enforced); get_entity/2 returns one by name within tenant. A definition from tenant A is invisible to tenant B.

Tenant isolation rides SetTenant + RLS on Loopctl.Repo for entity_definitions; the isolation TEST must run under the non-owner app role (SET LOCAL ROLE loopctl_app / Repo.with_tenant), because RLS is ENABLE not FORCE and a superuser/owner connection bypasses the policy and would prove nothing.

A configurable per-tenant cap on entity definitions (and thus generated tools) is enforced at create time, so a tenant cannot inflate the dynamic ListTools payload/latency without bound. Over-cap creation returns {:error, :entity_limit}.

Relationships are explicitly OUT of scope for v1 and are NOT persisted (no unvalidated relationship JSON is stored). A note records that any future relationship/join traversal must add per-join tenant scoping + target-entity-must-be-allowlisted validation before it ships.

The migration creates entity_definitions AND calls enable_rls(:entity_definitions) (like every other tenant table); the down migration cleanly drops it. Migrations run green on a fresh DB and pass the rollback test.

test_cases.name: create + fetch an entity definition within tenant
steps: insert an Entity for the stories source with allowlisted fields [%{name: "status", type: :string, filterable: true, searchable: false}]
expected_results: the entity is returned with its fields; unique-per-tenant enforced

test_cases.name: changeset rejects non-allowlisted column, unsafe name, unknown source
steps: build Entity changeset declaring field {name: "tenant_id"} (not in the stories allowlist)
expected_results: all invalid: column-not-allowlisted error; identifier-regex error; backing_source not-allowlisted error

test_cases.name: entity definitions are tenant-isolated (proven under the app role)
preconditions: queries run under SET LOCAL ROLE loopctl_app
expected_results: tenant_b sees no entities; tenant_a sees its one; the test fails if run as owner (RLS actually enforced)

test_cases.name: entity cap is enforced
preconditions: tenant at the configured entity cap
steps: attempt to create one more entity

test_cases.name: migration up/down is reversible and enables RLS
steps: run the migration up then down
expected_results: entity_definitions created with RLS enabled on up; cleanly dropped on down; no orphaned objects

technical_notes: fields is {:array, :map} with per-element changeset validation (the codebase has NO embedded_schema/embeds_many anywhere; match Story.acceptance_criteria = {:array, :map}).
Per-source column allowlist is a server code constant keyed by backing_source; the source of truth for what any entity may expose. Validate at define time (here) AND execute time (US-30.3).
Backing sources v1: projects (Loopctl.Projects.Project), stories (Loopctl.WorkBreakdown.Story), epics — loopctl-internal only.
Field-name regex ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$ is defense-in-depth; the allowlist is the real control.
RLS: migration must enable_rls(:entity_definitions) (RlsHelpers, ENABLE not FORCE); isolation tests MUST run under the non-owner app role or they silently pass.
Relationships deferred out of v1 (not persisted) — avoids dead unguarded JSON that a later join feature could turn into a cross-tenant hole.
